read.description: Read a text file as `anchor│content` rows (4-letter, case-sensitive anchors). Edit by anchor, never by content or line number. `offset`: 1-indexed line or a served anchor (then `limit` counts lines from that row). Page long files with offset/limit; on truncation continue from the hinted offset. A stale anchor is refused with fresh rows. Images attach visually; binary, directories and UTF-16/32 are rejected; an empty file returns one empty row to replace.

ask_user.description: Ask the user one or more questions as an interactive form (choice or free text). Use it whenever you need their decision, preference or input — never type questions inline. Grilling/design-interview rounds (Q1..QN, ❓, 'recommended answer') MUST go through ask_user.

params.properties.questions.items.properties.al: Choice only: allow free text (default true)
params.properties.questions.items.properties.re: Your recommended answer; highlights the matching option, else shown as a hint
params.properties.questions: Questions shown together in one form
params.properties.numbered: Prefix Q1, Q2… (grilling rounds only). Default false.

todo.description:
Phased todo list.
- `task`/`phase` are verbatim content strings, never generated ids ("task-1"); keep them stable; `view` if you lost the exact text.
- ops: `init` {list:[{phase,items}]} or {items} (replaces the list) · `start`/`done`/`drop`/`block` {task|phase, reason?}/`unblock` · `rm` {task?|phase?} (neither clears all) · `append` {phase,items} (creates the phase) · `view`.
- Tasks: 5–10 words, what not how. Phases: short noun phrase, no "1."/"Phase 1:" prefix.
- With nothing in progress, completing a task promotes the earliest open one; completed tasks never revert.
- `block` tasks awaiting the user, another agent or a service (skips the stop reminder); if you can clear the blocker, `append` a task for it instead.
- Create a list for 3+ steps, when asked, for a given task set, or when new instructions arrive mid-task. A user's plan, checklist or "N items" MUST be `init`ed one task per item — never merge, sample or drop items.
- Mark done immediately; complete phases in order; never make todo the only tool call of a turn.

bg_task.description: Run shell commands in the background without blocking the turn: persistent logs, no default timeout, stopped as a process group, can wake you on exit or matching output. Recognized bash monitoring loops are auto-diverted here.

params.properties.notifyMode: always = every update; transition = only when the output tail changes; first-match-only = one notifyPattern match. Default: first-match-only with notifyPattern, else transition.

replace.description: Replace a line range by anchor: `remove_from`/`remove_to` are the anchors of its first and last line (the same anchor for one line; `replace_from`/`replace_to` are aliases); `text` is the exact replacement. Deleting every line empties the file and returns its empty-line anchor for seeding. To change part of a line, use `replace_match`.

params.properties.text: Exact replacement; "" deletes the range. A trailing newline sets the last line's terminator (no extra blank line); a lone newline writes one blank line.

replace_match.description: Change a fragment inside a line range without retyping the rest. `replace_from`/`replace_to`: anchors of the first and last line searched (the same anchor for one line; `remove_from`/`remove_to` are aliases). Both boundary rows must still match what was served; interior lines are searched as on disk. Every occurrence of `match` in the range becomes `replacement`; everything else stays byte-for-byte. Copy `match` from a served row and send only the fragment that changes; it must be unique within the range, not file-wide — to change one of several occurrences, narrow the anchors instead of lengthening `match`. If `match` would be the whole line minus indentation and trailing punctuation, use `replace`.

params.properties.replace_from: Anchor of the FIRST line searched.
params.properties.replace_to: Anchor of the LAST line searched (= replace_from for one line).
params.properties.match: Exact fragment that changes, within one line. A trailing newline counts as the line's terminator; any other newline, or a value that is only a newline, is refused.
params.properties.replacement: Exact replacement for every match; "" deletes them. One line; a trailing newline is dropped.

params.properties.text: Exact text without anchor prefixes, never including the anchor line; "" inserts one blank line. A trailing newline sets the last line's terminator; a lone newline writes one blank line.

copy.description: Duplicate a line range (`source_from`..`source_to`; the same anchor for one line) before or after `anchor`, in this or another file. It copies the content as served, so same-message edits to the source don't change it. Source anchors stay live; the copy gets fresh anchors in the post-edit diff and keeps its line endings.

move.description: Relocate a line range before or after `anchor`, in this or another file. Within one file the destination must lie outside the range; moving it onto itself reports `No changes made`. A cross-file move commits on its own when its source file has other batched edits, does not show the source diff, and leaves the source needing a read for fresh anchors.

grep.description: Search with ripgrep. Hits are `N:│ anchor│content`, context rows `N-│ anchor│content`; both are editable without a read, under `=== path ===` headers. Regex by default (Rust syntax: no backreferences or look-around); `literal: true` for exact text or regex metacharacters, `ignoreCase`, `context` for surrounding rows. Respects .gitignore, skips .git, binaries and images. Matches over 500 bytes show as a fragment; the anchor still covers the line. Cut by match limit: raise `limit` (default 100); cut by size: narrow `pattern` or `path`.

params.properties.glob: Glob filter; `*` crosses directories (e.g. `*.ts`); relative to the search root.

web_search.description: Search the web; returns source-linked results or provider answers. Full results are stored for get_search_content via the returned responseId. Omit provider unless overriding the configured default.

params.properties.queries: 2–4 queries searched concurrently. Vary angle, scope and phrasing — near-duplicates waste results.
params.properties.provider: Override the configured provider (one name or a list searched together). Omit to use the default.
params.properties.workflow: none (default) | summary-review (curator with draft summary) | auto-summary (summary, no curator)
params.properties.proxy: http(s)/socks proxy URL for every request in this call, when direct access is blocked; "" forces direct.

params.properties.provider: Override the configured provider (one name or a list searched together).
params.properties.proxy: http(s)/socks proxy URL for this call; "" forces direct.

fetch_content.description: Fetch URL(s) as markdown (`readable`, default), the exact body over direct HTTP (`raw`), or an answer to `prompt` from the fetched content only (`answer`). Handles direct images, GitHub repos (cloned locally), PDFs, YouTube and local videos. Full content is stored for get_search_content.

params.properties.forceClone: Clone GitHub repos above the size threshold
params.properties.prompt: Question for answer mode or video analysis
params.properties.answerModel: provider/model override for answer mode (default: configured answer model, else the current model)
params.properties.timestamp: Video frame(s): '1:23:45', '23:45', '85' (seconds), or a range '23:41-25:00' giving a contact sheet of evenly spaced frames (default 6) — use a range when you know roughly where. Needs ffmpeg (+ yt-dlp for YouTube).
params.properties.frames: Frame count: with a range sets density; with one timestamp, N frames 5s apart; alone, samples the whole video.
params.properties.model: Gemini model override for video analysis
params.properties.auth: authFetch browser-cookie profile name (true when exactly one exists)
params.properties.proxy: http(s)/socks proxy URL when the target is unreachable directly; "" forces direct.
params.properties.redirects: Refuse cross-origin redirects (scheme, host and port must match)

params.properties.limit: Max characters (default and max: maxInlineContentChars); ignored with findText
params.properties.findText: Text(s) to locate in the stored content; overrides offset/limit

bg_wait.description:
Wait for background work that has no native wake (provider, detached); async subagent runs already wake this session.
{} first to finish or need attention · {all:true} all active work · {id} one run (returns result references) · {id,nonBlocking:true} subscribe and return now.
A timeout or user message ends the wait without error; work keeps running.

tern_status.description: Report Tern state: pane ids, TSP hello (kinds, features, credits), last mermaid, mirror state; `manifest` adds the capability contract. Other tern_* tools are callable from codemode by name: capture, panes, ctl, mirror, watch, diagnose, shot, remote, bridge, doc, board, carly, notebook, settings, chart, worktree, pr, fleet.

tern_run.description: Run a shell command in a visible Tern pane and return its output; `fromTranscript` runs the newest bash/sh block from the conversation. Runs with pi's permissions.

tool_search.description: Search deferred tools (such as MCP server tools) with BM25 and load the matches for your next call. Always use it to find MCP tools.

lines: Use the hashline tools for every file read and edit: read, replace, replace_match, insert, copy, move, undo_last_change.
Post-edit diff `+`/` ` rows and served rows already carry fresh anchors; re-read only for anchors you lack. `replace_match` needs both boundary rows served.

replace/replace_match/insert/copy/move: same-message calls need disjoint ranges; same-file calls commit as one batch (earlier calls reply `In batch N (queued)`, the last shows the combined diff, one undo reverts all). An invalid call fails alone; a failure while the batch runs aborts it.
replace/replace_match/insert/copy/move: anchors pick the file; `path` is optional but must match. In post-edit diffs `-anchor│` rows are dead, `+anchor│` and ` anchor│` rows live.
replace/replace_match/insert: `text` is written verbatim; escapes decode once at parse (`\uXXXX` is the character, `\\uXXXX` the literal text).
replace: `text: ""` is the cheap way to clear a large range (checks only its first and last line).

copy/move: only the two source boundary rows and the destination line need serving. To land right beside the block, anchor its last line with `after` (or first with `before`); to append at end of file, anchor the file's last line with `after`. An empty destination file is seeded.
undo_last_change: one slot per file, not a stack (a second undo returns E_UNDO_NONE); a `write` clears it; a cross-file move needs an undo on both files.

ask_user: put all related questions of a turn in one call; set `numbered: true` only for grilling rounds. Forms need TUI or RPC (print/json mode returns plain text). On 'cancelled', stop and let the user redirect.

bg_task: use it instead of nohup/& or foreground polling loops for long commands and for tmux/session/agent/log monitoring; check with list/log/stop. If a bash monitor gets auto-backgrounded, carry on and check it later.
Prefer the lsp_* tools for known symbols, definitions, references, types, diagnostics and call sites; grep for exact literals.

grep.text: Ripgrep search; hits are editable anchored rows

replace_match.text: Replace a fragment within lines by anchor

insert.text: Insert lines before/after an anchor line

ask_user.text: Ask the user through an interactive form

source_check.text: Gather cited sources for a claim

fetch_content.text: Fetch URLs, GitHub repos, PDFs, images, videos

get_search_content.text: Read stored web_search/fetch_content results by responseId

todo-discipline.description: How to keep the todo tool's phased list live: init before work, one task per item, mark done immediately.
